title: Canonical derived etale-Zariski adjunction data
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with site objects in universe $u+1$ and morphisms and structure-module sections in universe $u$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the canonical Zariski/small-etale ringed-site tensor-extension and restriction adjunction $L_c\dashv R_c$, presented by a context $c$ consisting of continuity and right-adjoint-existence proofs [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square]. The structure-module map $L_c\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ is the canonical adjoint scalar-multiplication map of this adjunction. Choose the unbounded derived localizations and their homotopy-category localization functors $Q_h$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] [def-pc-derived-category]. Derived etale-Zariski equivalence data on $T$ consists of: such a context $c$; additivity proofs for $L_c,R_c$; preservation of finite limits and colimits and faithfulness of $L_c$; functors $L:D(\mathcal O_T)\to D(\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}})$ and $R$ in the reverse direction; an isomorphism $Q_h L\simeq K(L_c)Q_h$ identifying $L$ with termwise tensor extension; a transformation $\rho:K(R_c)Q_h\to Q_hR$ making $R$ the right derived functor of $R_c$, with $\rho$ invertible on K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex]; and an adjunction $L\dashv R$. The derived adjunction is normalized on homotopy representatives: for $t:K(L_c)P\to I$, transposing the composite $L(Q_hP)\to Q_h(K(L_c)P)\to Q_hI$ supplied by the factorization isomorphism and $Q_h(t)$ gives $Q_h$ of the ordinary adjunction transpose of $t$, followed by $\rho_I$. The canonical structure-module map is required to be invertible. Quasi-coherence of cohomology on the Zariski side means [pqf-def-coherent] in each degree, and on the small etale side means [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] in each degree. Both $L$ and $R$ preserve these quasi-coherent cohomology properties, and the actual derived adjunction unit and counit are isomorphisms on the respective quasi-coherent cohomology subcategories. This defines a type of data, not a theorem asserting its existence; $L$ and $R$ have the whole unbounded derived categories as domains.
